question.text: Let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from focus $S$ of hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ on the line $b x-a y=0$ and let $C$ be the centre of the hyperbola. Then, the area of the rectangle whose sides are equal to that of $S P$ and $C P$ is

solution.text: Given, equation of hyperbola is $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ From figure, $\begin{aligned} S P &=\mid \frac{a b e}{\sqrt{b^{2}+a^{2}}} \\ &=\left|\frac{a b e}{a e}\right|=b \end{aligned}$ and $C S=a e$ Again, $\Delta S P C$ is right angled triangle at $P$. $$ \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad C P &=\sqrt{C S^{2}-S P^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{a^{2} e^{2}-b^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{a^{2}\left(1+\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}\right)-b^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-b^{2}}=a \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ Area of rectangle $=C P \times S P$ $=a b$
